survey.question: Which window layout is authoritative for v1?
options: Canonical 'Rectify Window': 3-tab side panel (Notes/Payload/History), bezel-less mirror
Earlier 'Rectify Window v1': single Annotations+Payload panel, black-bezel device frame, no History tab
survey.answer: As shown in the design ("такий як на дизайні") — resolved to the canonical 'Rectify Window' 3-tab layout, since every one of the 16 catalog screens (Rectify Screens.dc.html) imports `dc-import name="Rectify Window"` exclusively; none of the 16 reference 'Rectify Window v1'. That earlier file is a superseded iteration, not used by any in-scope screen.

data.problemStatement: Developers and QA testers who spot visual/UI bugs on a connected Android device (or iOS device in v1.1+) have no fast, structured way to hand precise, measurement-rich bug context (exact region, pixel/dp gaps, underlying view-hierarchy node) to a locally running Claude Code coding agent, and no built-in way to confirm a fix actually landed without manually re-testing the same spot by hand.

problems.text: Reporting a UI bug today means manually screenshotting, describing position/size in prose, and losing precise measurement/hierarchy context — producing slow, ambiguous handoffs to a coding agent.
There is no closed loop: after a coding agent claims a fix, the reporter must manually re-open the app and eyeball the same spot, with no diff against the original bug frame.
Visual bug triage across Android (adb/scrcpy) and iOS (idb/simctl) today requires manual device wrangling with no single tool bridging device mirroring, annotation, and agent handoff.
An existing local MCP server (`rectify`, exposing `get_latest_annotation`) already anticipates a structured handoff path, but no client currently produces or sends that structured payload.

personas.name: Mobile Developer
personas.description: Engineer running the app under test and a local Claude Code session against its repo; spots bugs while manually exercising the app and wants fixes applied with minimal back-and-forth.
needs: Annotate a bug precisely (box + measurement) without leaving the live device mirror
Send full visual + structural context to Claude Code in one action
Confirm a fix actually resolved the specific annotated issue before moving on

personas.name: QA Tester
personas.description: Tester running structured or exploratory passes on a device, often without direct repo access; relies on Rectify to hand off findings to a developer's running Claude Code session.
needs: Flag multiple bugs quickly during a single pass without losing context between them
Produce reports precise enough that a developer/agent doesn't need to re-ask what's wrong
See the status of previously reported batches (fixed / in progress) without re-testing everything

goals.text: Let a reporter capture a precise, measurement-rich UI bug (box, comment, optional dp/pixel gaps, hierarchy node) in seconds without leaving the live device mirror.
Close the loop between sending a bug report and confirming the fix, without requiring manual re-testing of the same UI region.
Reduce back-and-forth between bug reporter and coding agent by delivering one structured payload (screenshot, crops, hierarchy XML, prompt) per send.
Provide a reliable local handoff mechanism to a running Claude Code session via the existing `rectify` MCP server.
Deliver a complete Android-first v1 workflow (mirror -> annotate -> measure -> send -> verify), with iOS deferred to v1.1+.

nonGoals: Cloud sync, multi-user accounts, or any auth/login model in v1
iOS mirroring and iOS-specific flows in v1 (deferred to v1.1+)
Automated bug fixing or code generation inside Rectify itself (fixing happens in the Claude Code agent, not in Rectify)

successMetrics.text: Time from spotting a bug to Claude Code receiving the structured report.
Share of sent batches that reach a 'Fixed' status confirmed by one Verify cycle.
Verify false-positive rate (marks a batch resolved when the issue persists).
First-attempt device-connect success rate (adb/idb detection through live mirror start) for supported setups.

functionalRequirements.text: On launch, detect installed adb and idb tool versions and show a status dot per platform in the toolbar.
Show a platform switch (Android/iOS) in the toolbar on every screen; Android is functional in v1, iOS is deferred to v1.1+.
Provide a device picker dropdown with Physical-device and Emulator sections (running, or shut-down with an inline Boot button), navigable via arrow keys and Enter.
Provide a primary 'Start mirroring' action that connects to the selected device and begins the live mirror stream.
When no device is connected, poll adb every 2s and show a 'NO SIGNAL' empty state with guidance to plug in a USB-debug device or boot an emulator inline.
Support click-and-drag on the live mirror to draw a selection box, rendering a dashed red outline, a live device-pixel size label, and ruler/tick coordinate guides during the drag.
On drag release, freeze the exact current frame and create a new staged annotation anchored to the drawn box.

On a frozen frame, dim everything outside annotation boxes and show a per-annotation popover with a numbered badge, an autofocused free-text comment field (placeholder 'What's wrong here?'), a delete control, and a size/position meta line; Enter saves, clicking the delete control removes the annotation.
When annotation popovers would crowd/overlap, relocate them to a gutter/sidebar panel connected to their boxes via leader lines.

While holding Option over an annotation box, enter Measure mode: snap to the matched underlying view-hierarchy node, show dashed guide boxes for neighboring views and dp/pixel gap measurements in a floating 'Measuring' panel, highlight misalignment in red, and attach the measurement data to that annotation's note (prefixed with the Option symbol).
Use the canonical 'Rectify Window' layout: a bezel-less live mirror with a side panel exposing exactly three tabs (Notes, Payload, History).
In the Payload tab's Prompt section, show the auto-generated text prompt, its token-count estimate, and an Edit affordance.
In the Payload tab's Crops section, show a 3-column grid of per-annotation cropped images with the red outline baked in, each captioned 'from frame <id>'.
In the Payload tab's Hierarchy section, show a monospace, indented view-hierarchy tree with matched/flagged nodes visually marked.
Show a Payload footer summarizing contents ('frame.png · N crops · hierarchy.xml') and total payload size.

In the toolbar, show a staged-annotation counter, a 'Clear' action that removes all staged annotations, and a primary 'Resolve & Send' button that is disabled while zero annotations are staged or while a send is in progress.

On 'Resolve & Send', package the full frame screenshot, per-annotation crops, view-hierarchy XML dump, and generated prompt, and transmit them to the locally running Claude Code agent via the local 'rectify' MCP server (e.g. for retrieval through a `get_latest_annotation`-style tool).

During send, show a visible status sequence (Streaming -> Frozen -> Dumping hierarchy -> Sent) with colored dots, then confirm with a toast ('Sent N annotations to Claude Code · frame + hierarchy · <time>s') including an 'Open session' link.
After a successful send, resume live mirroring automatically and reset the staged-annotation counter to 0.
Provide a History tab listing every batch ever sent, grouped by time period, each row showing a thumbnail crop, title/summary, timestamp, and a status chip (e.g. Fixed, In progress).

On batches with status 'Fixed', provide a 'Verify' action that re-captures the live screen and diffs it, per annotation box, against the original frozen frame; matches mark the annotation resolved, mismatches surface a one-click follow-up that re-stages that single annotation for re-send.
Show a status bar with live stream stats: tool version, resolution, fps, and latency.

Render structured error-card states (icon-in-circle, title, body, optional copyable command block, primary+secondary actions, footer diagnostic line) for: adb not in PATH, no device detected, and multiple devices connected (with an inline device list/picker instead of a modal, defaulting the primary action to the top-listed device).

On a mid-session stream drop, show a non-blocking floating banner over the stale mirror ('Stream dropped' / 'Your N annotations are kept on the frozen frame' / 'Reconnect'); staged annotations stay pinned and 'Resolve & Send' remains usable while disconnected.
(v1.1+) Support iOS simulator/device mirroring via idb+simctl, including simulator-not-booted and device-not-trusted error-card states.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Live mirror glass-to-glass latency should stay low enough (target under ~150ms) that drag-to-select and freeze feel responsive.
Measure-mode hierarchy-node lookup on Option-hover should resolve in under ~100ms so the measuring panel feels instantaneous.
Resolve & Send payload transmission to the local MCP server should typically complete in under ~2s on localhost for a typical batch.
All mirror stream data, screenshots, hierarchy dumps, and payloads stay local to the machine; no network egress beyond localhost MCP communication.
adb/idb commands are only ever invoked against the user's explicitly selected, connected device — never an arbitrary or remote target.
Stream-drop handling must preserve all staged annotations without loss across a disconnect/reconnect cycle.
History and batch metadata persist locally and survive app restarts.
Device picker, annotation popovers, and error-card actions are fully keyboard-navigable (arrow keys/Enter for pickers, Enter/Escape for popovers).
All screens support full light and dark theme parity using the defined signal-color system (red = bug, green = fixed, orange = warning, blue = measurement) with sufficient contrast in both themes.
v1 targets macOS only; no Windows/Linux builds.
Token-count estimation for the generated prompt computes without perceptible delay (target under ~200ms) before Resolve & Send is enabled.
The payload format (prompt + crops + hierarchy XML) is versioned so the receiving MCP server/Claude Code agent can evolve its parsing without breaking older sends.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given adb and idb are installed, when the app launches, then the toolbar shows a status dot reflecting detected tool versions for both platforms.
Given a physical device is connected and an emulator is running, when the device picker is opened, then both appear in distinct Physical/Emulator sections and arrow keys plus Enter select an entry.
Given a device is selected in the picker, when the user clicks 'Start mirroring', then the live mirror begins streaming.
Given no device is connected, when adb polling runs, then the 'NO SIGNAL' state shows with guidance text and an inline emulator picker plus Boot button.
Given live mirror is streaming, when the user drags on the mirror, then a dashed red outline, live pixel-size label, and ruler guides render in real time.
When the user releases the drag, then the exact frame is frozen and a new staged annotation is created anchored to the drawn box.
Given a frozen frame with one annotation, then everything outside the box dims and a popover with numbered badge, autofocused comment field, delete control, and meta line appears.
Given an annotation popover is focused, when the user presses Enter, then the comment saves; when the user clicks the delete control, then the annotation is removed and the staged count decrements.
Given three annotations are drawn close together, when their popovers would overlap, then they relocate to a sidebar/gutter panel connected via leader lines.

Given a frozen frame with an annotation box, when the user holds Option over it, then the tool snaps to the matched view-hierarchy node and shows neighbor guide boxes with dp gap measurements in a 'Measuring' panel.

Given a measured element has misalignment (e.g. undersized hit target), then the offending dimension is highlighted in red and the note is prefixed with the Option-mode marker and carries the measurement data.
Given the canonical window layout is confirmed, then the side panel exposes exactly three tabs: Notes, Payload, History, over a bezel-less mirror.
Given at least one staged annotation exists, when the user opens the Payload tab, then a generated text prompt with token-count estimate and an Edit affordance is shown.
Given staged annotations exist, when viewing Payload > Crops, then a 3-column grid shows each annotation's cropped image with its red outline baked in and caption 'from frame <id>'.
Given staged annotations exist, when viewing Payload > Hierarchy, then a monospace indented tree displays with matched/flagged nodes visually marked.
Given the Payload tab is open, then its footer summarizes 'frame.png · N crops · hierarchy.xml' plus a total size that matches the actual payload.
Given zero annotations are staged, then 'Resolve & Send' is disabled; given one or more are staged, it is enabled; 'Clear' removes all staged annotations and resets the counter to 0.

When the user clicks 'Resolve & Send', then the frame screenshot, per-annotation crops, hierarchy XML, and generated prompt are transmitted via the local MCP server such that a Claude Code session calling the retrieval tool receives the complete payload.

When sending, then the status sequence Streaming -> Frozen -> Dumping hierarchy -> Sent displays in order with colored dots, and on completion a toast shows the sent-count/time summary with an 'Open session' link.
While a send is in progress, 'Resolve & Send' is disabled and only re-enables after the toast confirms or the send fails.
After a successful send, then live mirroring resumes automatically and the staged-annotation counter resets to 0.
Given batches have been sent previously, when the History tab is opened, then batches are grouped by time period, each showing thumbnail, summary, timestamp, and status chip.

Given a batch has status 'Fixed', when the user clicks 'Verify', then the app re-captures the live screen and diffs it, per annotation box, against the stored frozen frame using a pixel-region diff plus a hierarchy/layout diff of the matched node.

Given a Verify diff finds no material difference for an annotation, then that annotation is marked resolved; given a difference remains, then a one-click follow-up re-stages only that annotation for re-send.
Given live mirror is active, then the status bar displays current tool version, resolution, fps, and latency, updating at least once per second.
Given adb is not found on PATH, then an error card renders with the install command (with Copy), primary 'Locate adb…' and secondary 'Retry' actions.
Given no Android device is detected after launch, then an error card renders with the kill-server command and primary 'Restart adb' / secondary 'Boot emulator instead' actions.
Given 3 devices are connected simultaneously, then the error card shows an inline device list (not a modal) and the primary action names the top device (e.g. 'Mirror Pixel 8 Pro').

Given the stream drops mid-session with staged annotations present, then a non-blocking banner appears stating the stream dropped and that annotations are kept on the frozen frame, with a 'Reconnect' primary action; 'Resolve & Send' remains clickable and annotations remain pinned throughout.
Given the user toggles light/dark theme, then all screens render correctly in both themes with consistent signal colors (red/green/orange/blue) and no unreadable contrast regions.

(v1.1+) Given iOS is selected as platform, when the simulator isn't booted, then an error card with 'Boot simulator' primary / 'Choose another' secondary renders; when the device isn't trusted, an error card with "I've tapped Trust — retry" primary / 'Use simulator' secondary renders.

assumptions.text: Only one device is mirrored at a time per session; switching devices clears or prompts to clear staged annotations.
History and batch metadata persist locally (e.g. local file/DB store) across app restarts; not synced to any cloud service.
Rectify is a fully local, single-user, no-auth desktop tool in v1; there is no account/login model.
v1 ships macOS-only; Windows and Linux are not supported.
iOS support (idb/simctl flows, including error screens for simulator-not-booted and device-not-trusted) ships in the v1.1+ milestone, not v1; Android is the v1 ground-truth platform.

[CONFIRMED via Stage 2 survey] The existing local 'rectify' MCP server and its get_latest_annotation-style tool are the sole mechanism by which the Claude Code agent retrieves sent payloads — no file-system or webhook fallback in v1.

[CONFIRMED via Stage 2 survey] The canonical 'Rectify Window' (3-tab Notes/Payload/History, bezel-less mirror) is the authoritative v1 window layout — it is the layout every one of the 16 catalog screens actually uses. 'Rectify Window v1' is a superseded earlier iteration and is out of scope.

constraints.text: Android mirroring/control depends on adb + scrcpy; iOS (v1.1+) depends on idb + simctl — both must be compatible with the user's installed Android SDK / Xcode toolchain.
View-hierarchy capture for measurement and the hierarchy dump is bounded by what each platform's inspection API exposes (e.g. uiautomator-style dump for Android).
Claude Code must be running locally with the 'rectify' MCP server available for Resolve & Send to have a receiving agent; Rectify is not a standalone bug tracker.
v1 scope is Android-first per confirmed decision; iOS mirroring and iOS-specific error screens (14, 15) are deferred to v1.1+.

Automated bug fixing or code generation inside Rectify itself

proposedSurvey.question: Which window layout is authoritative for v1?
options: Canonical 'Rectify Window': 3-tab side panel (Notes/Payload/History), bezel-less mirror
Earlier 'Rectify Window v1': single Annotations+Payload panel, black-bezel device frame, no History tab
proposedSurvey.recommended: Canonical 'Rectify Window': 3-tab side panel (Notes/Payload/History), bezel-less mirror
proposedSurvey.rationale: All 16 catalog screens — including the explicitly in-scope History and Verify screens — use the 3-tab canonical layout; the single-panel v1 design has no History tab at all, contradicting the confirmed in-scope screen inventory.

proposedSurvey.question: What is the transport/protocol for delivering a Resolve & Send payload to the Claude Code agent?
options: Local MCP server only — the existing 'rectify' MCP tool (e.g. get_latest_annotation) is the sole transport
MCP server plus a fallback mechanism (e.g. writing payload files to a known local path the agent can also read directly)
proposedSurvey.recommended: Local MCP server only — the existing 'rectify' MCP tool (e.g. get_latest_annotation) is the sole transport
proposedSurvey.rationale: An MCP server named 'rectify' already exists and exposes a retrieval tool; this is the simplest, most direct signal of intended integration and avoids building/maintaining a second transport without evidence it's needed.

proposedSurvey.question: What should the Verify action diff to decide if an annotation is resolved?
options: Pixel-region diff only, within the annotated box
Hierarchy/layout diff only, for the matched view node
Combination: pixel-region diff within the box plus hierarchy/layout diff of the matched node
proposedSurvey.recommended: Combination: pixel-region diff within the box plus hierarchy/layout diff of the matched node
proposedSurvey.rationale: Measure mode already captures and matches a hierarchy node per annotation, and many real UI bugs (misalignment, sizing) are structural rather than purely pixel-level; combining both diff types reduces false positives/negatives versus either alone.
